svg.title: The full Hecke-lisse category and its coefficient action
svg.desc: The ind-connection inclusion has a continuous right adjoint and coherent commuting coordinate coreflectors. Their kernels construct the full presentable Hecke-lisse category. Canonical tensor duality transposes the collision maps to a coalgebra, whose full Ran category acts on it. Its actual comparison with the restricted spectral category has an explicit remaining equivalence hypothesis. The projective-line diagonal and a two-factor category distinguish compactness and full faithfulness.
svg.text: The full Hecke-lisse category carries a coherent coefficient action
Complex curves; all genera and components; full unbounded automorphic categories.
1. The actual ind-connection coreflector and its coordinate images — HLA.4–HLA.9
i : I → D(X), i ⊣ g, g i = id; both i and g preserve colimits.
g(N)(P) = RHom in D(X) from i(P) to N, for every compact finite-connection P.
p = i g; p → id → q₀; ker(q₀) = I, also after every independent tensor factor.
The pⱼ commute with their actual counits; intersection of the images = W ⊗ I⊗ᴶ.
Membership requires every counit to be an equivalence, not just a nonzero projection.
2. A full presentable kernel retains every Hecke coordinate — HLA.10–HLA.16
M(Hl) = intersection over V of ker[(id ⊗ q₀) H(V)].
Large κ-compact approximations and countable killing chains prove presentability.
The exchange maps put each coordinate in I; commuting coreflectors put all of them there.
H(vec V) : M(Hl) → M(Hl) ⊗ I⊗ᴶ, with all unit, collision and higher maps.
Integrating against any full parameter D-module preserves M(Hl): actual Ran stability.
3. Tensor duality gives the correct coefficient coalgebra — HLA.17–HLA.22
Γ(I)(E) = RHom(I)(1,E); ev(E,F) = Γ(I)(E ⊗ F); hence I ≃ I∨.
The transpose of i is g: ev(I)(E,gN) = p_*(iE ⊗! N).
δ(I) is the transpose of lisse tensor multiplication, with counit Γ(I).
(g ⊗ g) Δ_* = δ(I) g; all finite-set maps, including unused coordinates, agree.
The ambient diagonal itself need not preserve lisse objects.
4. Full coefficient Ran action and the actual spectral comparison — HLA.23–HLA.30
R(I) = colim over ψ : I → J of Rep(H)⊗ᴵ ⊗ I(X)⊗ᴶ.
Its transition functors use δ(I); large-κ DG relations retain every stage and coherence.
Q(Ran) : R → R(I); Φ on M(Hl) = Φ(I) composed with Q(Ran).
L(I) : R(I) → A is the universal-coefficient functor, and L(I) Q(Ran) = L.
If L(I) is an equivalence, the actual idempotent is the identity on M(Hl).
That equivalence and the nilpotent-support/regularity criteria require separate proofs.
5. On P¹ the transposed diagonal is not compact — HLA.34–HLA.37
I = Mod(E), E=C[η]/η², |η|=2; R=E⊗E=C[x,y]/(x²,y²).
δ(I)(1) = E as an R-module via x=y=η.
Free eₙ has degree n; d eₙ = (x−y)eₙ₋₁ for odd n, (x+y)eₙ₋₁ for even n.
E ⊗ derived over R with C = direct sum of C[−n], for every n ≥ 0.
Thus δ(I)(1) is not compact. The full ambient Δ_*ω(X) is compact and not lisse.
(g ⊗ g)(Δ_*ω(X)) = δ(I)(1): the continuous g does not preserve all compacts.
6. A section and idempotence alone do not give full faithfulness — HLA.38–HLA.40
C = Vect × Vect; L(U,V)=U; G(U)=(U,U); F=GL.
L G = id and F²=F, but Hom(GU,GV) = Hom(U,V) ⊕ Hom(U,V).
G sends f to (f,f); the endomorphism (id,0) is missing from its image.
F(id,0)=(id,id): its restriction to the full essential image is not the identity.
The geometric image argument needs the actual module factorization and natural maps.
Exact proofs: §§3.205–3.216, HLA.1–HLA.40; Solutions3.DM–3.DO.
Lisse spectral-decomposition framework: AGKRRV, arXiv:2010.01906v2.
